principle: Interior spaces exist because ship systems, staffing, mission and habitation require them. A deck plan is a functional topology before it is scenery.

very_small_craft.rule: Combine functions aggressively; no assumption of dedicated bridge, sickbay, lab or quarters.

small_ship.rule: Dedicated bridge/control and engineering likely; medical/science/habitation scale to mission and endurance.

medium_multimission.rule: Dedicated departments and multiple support spaces become plausible; mission configuration decides lab/cargo/security emphasis.

large_explorer_or_capital.rule: Multiple redundant/departmental spaces, larger habitation and specialist facilities; civilians/passengers only if actual ship population state supports them.

topology_rules: Class/configuration defines possible baseline locations and connections.
Damage blocks runtime connections without rewriting baseline layout.
Access and clearance are runtime layers on top of physical connectivity.
Refits may add/remove spaces only through explicit topology version change.
ai_boundary: AI cannot teleport characters between interior locations.
AI cannot create a holodeck, lounge, brig, lab or transporter room merely because it is convenient.
AI cannot know occupants behind inaccessible/unknown areas without sensor/knowledge support.
visual_nap: Functional architecture precedes stylistic skin such as Pike/TOS/TNG.
Console design must follow operational function already defined by gameplay.
